title: Practise 9 more growth structuring questions, then compare your answers with model structures
description: 9 more growth case prompts (set 2) to structure in two minutes each, with model answers, where to start and the trap to avoid.
hook: Reading about structuring only gets you so far. The skill comes from doing it, many times, with a clock running. Here are 9 real growth prompts. For each one, give yourself two minutes to sketch a structure on paper, say where you would start, then open the model answer and compare. Do not worry about matching it exactly; look for what you missed.
body:
1. How can a football club make money from its stadium on non-match days?

Show a model structure
  • Events: Concerts, other sports; Conferences and weddings
  • Tourism: Stadium tours, museum; Shop and café
  • Property: Hotel, offices, housing on the site; Car parks and retail units
  • Community: Community sports pitches, gyms, schools; Partners and sponsors

Where to start: Events: concerts bring the largest revenue per day.

The trap: Ignoring the pitch damage and costs of big events.

2. How can a department store grow online sales from 15% to 30% of total?

Show a model structure
  • Traffic: Search, marketing, app; Existing store customers
  • Conversion: Range online, photos, stock accuracy; Checkout and delivery options
  • Stores as part of online: Click-and-collect, returns in store; Stock from stores
  • Repeat: Loyalty, personal offers; Delivery subscriptions

Where to start: Stores as part of online: department stores win with click-and-collect.

The trap: Treating online as a separate business from the stores.

3. How can a hotel group get more guests to book directly instead of through booking sites?

Show a model structure
  • Price and perks: Best rate on our site, member rates; Free breakfast, upgrades
  • Website and app: Ease of booking, speed; Search visibility
  • Loyalty: Points, recognition; Converting booking-site guests at the hotel
  • Channel terms: Commission levels; Rate rules with booking sites

Where to start: Converting booking-site guests during their stay costs least.

The trap: Cutting booking sites off before direct bookings can replace them.

4. How can a family farm raise its income by 50%?

Show a model structure
  • Yields and costs: Output per hectare; Fertiliser, fuel, machinery sharing
  • Prices: Selling direct, contracts; Premium: organic, local
  • Diversify: Farm shop, tourism, events; Renewable energy on land
  • Support: Grants, environmental payments; Co-operatives

Where to start: Diversify: on small farms, land-based side businesses often pay best.

The trap: Only trying to grow more of the same crop.

5. How can a broadband provider cut customer churn by a third?

Show a model structure
  • Find who will leave: End of contract, price rises; Speed problems, complaints
  • Fix the service: Network speed and outages; Installation and support
  • Keep them: Retention offers, contracts; Bundles with TV and mobile
  • Win back: Offers to recent leavers; Making cancelling clear but caring

Where to start: Find who will leave: target offers before the contract ends.

The trap: Giving discounts to everyone, including customers who weren't leaving.

6. How can a free personal-finance app start making money?

Show a model structure
  • Charge users: Premium subscription; Paid features: advice, reports
  • Partners: Commission on loans, savings, insurance; Switching services
  • Business customers: Sell the tool to employers; Data insights (with consent)
  • Costs and trust: Keep users' trust; Regulation

Where to start: Partners: commission on financial products is the usual model.

The trap: Selling user data in ways that destroy trust.

7. How can a bank grow its lending to small businesses by 25%?

Show a model structure
  • Reach: Existing customers who don't borrow; New businesses via partners
  • Decision speed: Time to approve; Automated credit checks
  • Products: Overdrafts, loans, invoice finance; Pricing vs rivals
  • Risk: Credit losses; Limits by sector

Where to start: Existing customers who don't borrow: the easiest to lend to safely.

The trap: Lowering credit standards to hit the target.

8. How can a software company grow revenue from its existing customers by 20%?

Show a model structure
  • More users: Seats in each account; Other teams in the same company
  • Higher plans: Upgrades to premium tiers; Add-on modules
  • Price: Annual price rises; Value-based pricing
  • Keep them: Churn and downgrades; Customer success

Where to start: More users: spreading to other teams is usually the biggest lever.

The trap: Pushing price rises without adding value.

9. How can a card-payments company win more small shops?

Show a model structure
  • Who we want: Types of shops, size; Those switching from cash
  • Offer: Fees, card readers, payout speed; Simple contracts
  • Channels: Online sign-up, partners, banks; Sales teams by region
  • Extra services: Lending to shops, booking, stock tools; Keeping shops once signed

Where to start: Offer: small shops care most about fees and getting paid quickly.

The trap: Only spending more on advertising.
outro: Come back to these in a week and try them again. You will be surprised how much quicker the structures come. Want more? The free structuring drill has a timer and over 100 prompts.
